title: CNS / Glioma Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides. Adult diffuse glioma pathway: workup -> maximal safe resection / biopsy -> WHO 2021 molecular class (IDH, 1p/19q) -> grade and risk -> subtype-directed induction (surgery/RT + concurrent chemo) -> restaging / response-adapted adjuvant -> surveillance, plus a line-of-therapy recurrence pathway (re-resection -> first salvage -> on progression -> later salvage). Systemic-therapy nodes now reference draft CNS dose protocols (cns-tmz-concurrent, cns-tmz-adjuvant, cns-pcv, cns-lomustine, cns-bevacizumab) so the recommended regimen opens in the Protocol Sheet with computed per-drug doses; the physician confirms and adjusts. Protocol doses are standard-of-care doses in the author's own wording, marked experimental / draft. No proprietary guideline text reproduced.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references (NCCN CNS, DeVita, Harrison) and WHO CNS5 (2021) molecular classification. Content authored in original wording. The referenced cns-* protocols carry standard-of-care regimen doses (temozolomide, PCV, lomustine, bevacizumab) authored in original wording as draft / experimental decision support, not copied from any source.

a.text: Stupp-type regimen: maximal safe resection followed by focal radiation with concurrent daily temozolomide, then adjuvant temozolomide cycles. Alternating electric-field therapy (TTFields) may be added in the adjuvant phase for supratentorial glioblastoma.

b.text: PCV = procarbazine, lomustine (CCNU), vincristine. Radiation followed by PCV is a standard chemoradiation backbone for 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma; some centers substitute temozolomide for tolerability.

c.text: Higher-risk lower-grade glioma is generally taken as age over ~40 or subtotal resection / residual disease (also large tumor, neurologic deficit, high proliferation). Such patients are offered postoperative radiation plus chemotherapy rather than observation.

d.text: MGMT promoter methylation predicts benefit from alkylating chemotherapy and is most decision-relevant in elderly / frailer glioblastoma, where it helps choose between temozolomide-containing therapy and radiation alone. It is prognostic but does not withhold Stupp therapy in fit patients.

e.text: Pseudoprogression is increased enhancement / edema within roughly 3 months of chemoradiation that later stabilizes or regresses without a change in therapy, and can mimic true progression. Short-interval MRI, perfusion imaging, or amino-acid PET help distinguish it; observation and steroid adjustment are preferred over premature salvage therapy.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and tissue diagnosis
nodes.description: Baseline evaluation of a suspected diffuse glioma before definitive management.
bullets: History, neurologic exam, performance status (KPS); document seizures, focal deficits, raised-ICP symptoms
Contrast MRI brain (structural); add perfusion / spectroscopy where it changes management (MR is the reference imaging)
Tissue diagnosis by maximal safe resection or biopsy for an integrated histologic + molecular diagnosis (WHO CNS5)
Molecular testing: IDH1/2 mutation, 1p/19q codeletion, ATRX, MGMT promoter methylation; add CDKN2A/B, EGFR, +7/-10, TERT for grading IDH-wildtype tumors
Perioperative supportive care: steroids for symptomatic edema, anti-seizure medication only if seizures, VTE awareness; multidisciplinary review

nodes.name: Clinical setting
nodes.title: Clinical setting
nodes.description: Choose the current scenario. Management branches by whether this is a new diagnosis, routine surveillance, or recurrence.

nodes.name: Resection
nodes.title: Maximal safe resection / biopsy
nodes.description: Extent of resection is both diagnostic and prognostic. Greater resection improves outcome when it can be achieved safely; otherwise biopsy secures the integrated diagnosis.
bullets: Aim for maximal safe cytoreduction within functional limits (awake mapping / intraoperative adjuncts as indicated)
Send tissue for integrated histologic + molecular classification
Extent of resection recorded (gross-total, subtotal, biopsy) - feeds risk stratification and adjuvant planning

nodes.name: Molecular class
nodes.title: WHO 2021 molecular class (IDH / 1p-19q)
nodes.description: Adult diffuse gliomas are classified first by IDH status and 1p/19q codeletion, which define three lineages and drive treatment more than histology alone.
bullets: Oligodendroglioma: IDH-mutant AND 1p/19q-codeleted (grade 2 or 3)
Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant: IDH-mutant, 1p/19q intact (grade 2, 3, or 4; CDKN2A/B homozygous loss upgrades to grade 4)
Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype: IDH-wildtype with molecular GBM features (EGFR amplification, +7/-10, or TERT promoter mutation; grade 4)
If IDH / 1p-19q are not yet back, defer adjuvant choice - it depends on the integrated diagnosis

tables.title: WHO CNS5 adult diffuse glioma classes

nodes.name: Await molecular
nodes.title: Molecular pending: defer adjuvant, optimize recovery
nodes.description: Integrated diagnosis not yet complete. Adjuvant therapy choice depends on IDH / 1p-19q, so defer it until results return.
bullets: Complete IDH, 1p/19q, MGMT, and grading markers before committing to adjuvant therapy
Continue supportive care; taper steroids as edema allows; treat seizures
Re-enter the class pathway once the integrated diagnosis is available
Do not start radiation or chemotherapy on histology alone when molecular results are imminent

nodes.name: Oligo grade
nodes.title: Oligodendroglioma: grade
nodes.description: Codeleted oligodendroglioma is graded 2 (lower-grade) or 3 (anaplastic). Grade and risk drive whether chemoradiation follows surgery.

nodes.name: Oligo G2 risk
nodes.title: Grade 2 oligodendroglioma: risk group
nodes.description: Lower-grade glioma is split into lower-risk (candidate for observation after resection) and higher-risk (postoperative chemoradiation).
bullets: Lower-risk: younger (about <= 40) AND gross-total / near-total resection, minimal residual, no major deficit
Higher-risk: age > 40, OR subtotal resection / residual disease, OR large tumor / neurologic deficit
Risk group, not grade alone, decides observe-versus-treat for grade 2 disease

nodes.name: Oligo G2 observe
nodes.title: Grade 2 oligodendroglioma, lower-risk: resection + observation
nodes.description: After maximal safe resection, close MRI observation is reasonable for lower-risk codeleted grade 2 disease, reserving radiation and chemotherapy for progression.
bullets: Maximal safe resection is the primary treatment
Serial MRI surveillance (for example every 3-6 months initially, then lengthen)
Defer radiation + PCV to documented progression or reclassification to higher-risk
Manage seizures; support neurocognition
nodes.linkLabel: On documented progression, enter the surveillance / recurrence pathway

nodes.name: Oligo G2 induction
nodes.title: Grade 2 oligodendroglioma, higher-risk: RT + PCV induction
nodes.description: Higher-risk codeleted grade 2 disease is treated with postoperative focal radiation followed by chemotherapy; proceed to restaging to guide the adjuvant course.
bullets: Focal external-beam radiation to the tumor bed
Followed by PCV (procarbazine, lomustine, vincristine); temozolomide is an alternative backbone at some centers
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts
Baseline and serial neurocognitive assessment

nodes.name: Oligo G3 induction
nodes.title: Grade 3 oligodendroglioma (anaplastic): RT + PCV induction
nodes.description: Anaplastic codeleted oligodendroglioma is treated with radiation plus chemotherapy after maximal safe resection - the codeletion predicts strong chemotherapy benefit. Restage to guide the adjuvant course.
bullets: Maximal safe resection, then focal radiation
Chemotherapy with PCV (preferred by long-term data); temozolomide is an alternative
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts
Serial neurocognitive assessment through therapy

nodes.name: Astro grade
nodes.title: Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant: grade
nodes.description: IDH-mutant astrocytoma is graded 2, 3, or 4 (CDKN2A/B homozygous loss defines grade 4). Grade drives the intensity of postoperative therapy.

nodes.name: Astro G2 risk
nodes.title: Grade 2 IDH-mutant astrocytoma: risk group
nodes.description: As with oligodendroglioma, lower-risk grade 2 astrocytoma may be observed after resection while higher-risk disease gets postoperative chemoradiation.
bullets: Lower-risk: age <= 40 and gross-total / near-total resection with minimal residual
Higher-risk: age > 40, or residual disease after subtotal resection / biopsy, or large / symptomatic tumor
IDH-mutant astrocytoma trends more aggressive than codeleted oligodendroglioma at equal grade

nodes.name: Astro G2 observe
nodes.title: Grade 2 IDH-mut astrocytoma, lower-risk: resection + observation
nodes.description: Maximal safe resection with MRI surveillance is reasonable for lower-risk grade 2 IDH-mutant astrocytoma.
bullets: Maximal safe resection is primary therapy
Serial MRI surveillance; reserve radiation + temozolomide for progression or reclassification
Manage seizures; support neurocognition
Any documented progression triggers restaging and treatment
nodes.linkLabel: On documented progression, enter the surveillance / recurrence pathway

nodes.name: Astro G2 induction
nodes.title: Grade 2 IDH-mut astrocytoma, higher-risk: RT + temozolomide induction
nodes.description: Higher-risk grade 2 IDH-mutant astrocytoma is treated with postoperative radiation followed by alkylating chemotherapy; restage to guide the adjuvant course.
bullets: Focal radiation to the tumor bed
Followed by alkylating chemotherapy (temozolomide; PCV is an alternative)
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts
Serial neurocognitive assessment

nodes.name: Astro G3 induction
nodes.title: Grade 3 IDH-mut astrocytoma (anaplastic): RT + temozolomide induction
nodes.description: Anaplastic IDH-mutant astrocytoma is treated with radiation plus temozolomide after maximal safe resection; restage to guide the adjuvant course.
bullets: Maximal safe resection, then focal radiation
Temozolomide (concurrent and/or adjuvant); PCV is an alternative alkylator backbone
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts
Serial neurocognitive assessment

nodes.name: Astro G4 induction
nodes.title: Grade 4 IDH-mut astrocytoma: Stupp-type induction
nodes.description: Grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma is treated like glioblastoma with a Stupp-type chemoradiation backbone, recognizing its more favorable biology than IDH-wildtype GBM; restage to guide the adjuvant course.
bullets: Maximal safe resection, then focal radiation with concurrent daily temozolomide
Adjuvant temozolomide cycles follow, guided by restaging
The Stupp-type regimen references the CNS draft dose protocols below (concurrent then adjuvant temozolomide), which compute doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts
Better prognosis than IDH-wildtype GBM but still treated intensively

nodes.name: GBM fitness
nodes.title: Glioblastoma: age / performance status
nodes.description: In IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, age and performance status choose between full Stupp therapy and an abbreviated elderly / frail regimen.
bullets: Fit: younger / good performance status (e.g. KPS >= 70), able to tolerate full chemoradiation
Elderly / frail: older (e.g. > 65-70) or poor performance status
MGMT methylation is most decision-relevant in the elderly / frail group

nodes.name: GBM Stupp induction
nodes.title: Glioblastoma, fit: Stupp chemoradiation induction (+/- TTFields)
nodes.description: Standard of care for fit IDH-wildtype glioblastoma is maximal safe resection followed by concurrent chemoradiation, given regardless of MGMT status; restage before adjuvant temozolomide.
bullets: Maximal safe resection
Focal radiation with concurrent daily temozolomide (induction), then plan adjuvant cycles after restaging
MGMT methylation is prognostic but does not withhold Stupp therapy in fit patients
The Stupp regimen references the CNS draft dose protocols below (concurrent then adjuvant temozolomide), which compute doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts

nodes.name: GBM elderly MGMT
nodes.title: Elderly / frail glioblastoma: MGMT status
nodes.description: In the elderly / frail glioblastoma, MGMT promoter methylation guides whether to use temozolomide-containing therapy or radiation alone with a hypofractionated schedule.

nodes.name: GBM elderly TMZ induction
nodes.title: Elderly GBM, MGMT methylated: hypofractionated RT + temozolomide induction
nodes.description: Methylated elderly glioblastoma benefits most from an alkylating agent; a hypofractionated radiation course with temozolomide (or temozolomide alone if radiation is not tolerable) is preferred, then restage.
bullets: Hypofractionated (short-course) radiation with concurrent temozolomide
Temozolomide alone is an option if radiation is not feasible (methylated tumors respond)
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts
Attention to marrow tolerance and performance status

nodes.name: GBM elderly chemoRT induction
nodes.title: Elderly GBM, MGMT unknown: hypofractionated RT + temozolomide induction
nodes.description: When MGMT status is unavailable, a hypofractionated radiation course with temozolomide is a pragmatic default for the elderly patient who can tolerate combined therapy; restage before adjuvant cycles.
bullets: Hypofractionated radiation with concurrent temozolomide
Send MGMT if not already done to refine the adjuvant choice
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts

nodes.name: GBM elderly RT
nodes.title: Elderly GBM, MGMT unmethylated: hypofractionated RT alone
nodes.description: Unmethylated elderly glioblastoma derives little from temozolomide; hypofractionated radiation alone is a reasonable, better-tolerated choice, with best supportive care for the frailest.
bullets: Hypofractionated radiation alone
Adding temozolomide gives limited benefit in unmethylated tumors
Best supportive care for the frailest / lowest performance status
Radiation-only pathway; no systemic dose protocol applies here

nodes.name: Restaging response
nodes.title: Restaging MRI after chemoradiation: response
nodes.description: After induction chemoradiation, a restaging MRI (typically ~4 weeks after radiation, then serially) is response-adapted: distinguish true response from pseudoprogression and from genuine early progression / residual disease. The answer drives the adjuvant course.
bullets: Responder: stable or reduced disease on restaging - proceed to planned adjuvant chemotherapy
Pseudoprogression: early increased enhancement / edema that is treatment effect, not true growth - continue therapy and re-image at short interval
True progression / residual: unequivocal growth or new disease during / just after induction - treat as refractory
Perfusion imaging or amino-acid PET, and short-interval re-imaging, help resolve ambiguous scans before changing therapy

nodes.name: Adjuvant continuation
nodes.title: Responder: adjuvant chemotherapy continuation
nodes.description: A responder proceeds to the planned adjuvant chemotherapy course after chemoradiation. Choose whether to add maintenance / device therapy or move to surveillance on completion.
bullets: Deliver the planned adjuvant alkylator cycles (e.g. temozolomide for astrocytoma / GBM, PCV for oligodendroglioma)
Monitor marrow counts, hepatic function, and performance status between cycles
Reassess with MRI before each restaging point; stop early for unequivocal progression
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts

nodes.name: Maintenance / TTFields
nodes.title: Adjuvant maintenance: TTFields / continued alkylator
nodes.description: Selected supratentorial glioblastoma patients add alternating electric-field therapy (TTFields) during maintenance, alongside continued adjuvant temozolomide, before transitioning to surveillance.
bullets: TTFields (alternating electric fields) added in the adjuvant phase for supratentorial glioblastoma
Continue adjuvant temozolomide cycles as planned
Manage scalp / skin care for the device; support adherence to wear-time
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts
nodes.linkLabel: Transition to high-grade surveillance on completion

nodes.name: Pseudoprogression
nodes.title: Suspected pseudoprogression: continue therapy, re-image
nodes.description: Findings favor treatment effect rather than true growth. Continue the planned adjuvant course and re-image at short interval rather than switching to salvage therapy prematurely.
bullets: Continue planned adjuvant chemotherapy; do not label as progression yet
Short-interval MRI (e.g. 4-8 weeks) with perfusion; consider amino-acid PET if available
Adjust steroids for symptomatic edema; avoid premature salvage therapy
If subsequent imaging confirms true growth, move to the recurrence pathway
nodes.linkLabel: If confirmed as true progression, enter the recurrence pathway

nodes.name: Early progression
nodes.title: True early progression / residual: treat as refractory
nodes.description: Unequivocal growth or residual disease during or just after chemoradiation is treated as refractory disease, managed on the recurrence / salvage pathway with a clinical trial prioritized.
bullets: Confirm true progression (perfusion / PET / short-interval MRI, biopsy if ambiguous)
Consider re-resection for symptomatic, accessible disease
Switch systemic therapy (alternate alkylator, bevacizumab for symptom control); prioritize a clinical trial
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts
nodes.linkLabel: Manage on the recurrence / salvage pathway

nodes.name: Surveillance type
nodes.title: Surveillance: tumor grade
nodes.description: Follow-up cadence differs by grade. Choose the treated tumor category.

nodes.name: LGG surveillance
nodes.title: Lower-grade glioma surveillance
nodes.description: Long-horizon MRI surveillance, since lower-grade gliomas progress slowly and can transform.
bullets: MRI at intervals (for example every 3-6 months for 5 years, then lengthen) - individualize
Watch for radiographic progression or new enhancement (possible transformation to higher grade)
Neurocognitive and seizure follow-up
A confirmed progression enters the recurrence pathway
nodes.linkLabel: On confirmed progression, enter the recurrence pathway

nodes.name: HGG surveillance
nodes.title: High-grade glioma / GBM surveillance
nodes.description: Closer MRI surveillance with awareness of pseudoprogression early after chemoradiation.
bullets: MRI roughly every 2-4 months (individualize) after completing chemoradiation
Distinguish pseudoprogression (early post-chemoradiation) from true progression - short-interval re-imaging / perfusion helps
Monitor steroid needs and performance status
A confirmed progression enters the recurrence pathway
nodes.linkLabel: On confirmed progression, enter the recurrence pathway

nodes.name: Recurrence type
nodes.title: Recurrence: tumor category
nodes.description: At recurrence, first confirm true progression (versus pseudoprogression / treatment effect), then select the category to guide salvage options.
bullets: Confirm true progression on MRI (+/- perfusion / spectroscopy or biopsy)
Re-review molecular class and prior therapy received (radiation, alkylator)
Prioritize a clinical trial at every salvage line

nodes.name: Recurrent LGG re-op
nodes.title: Recurrent lower-grade glioma: re-resection decision
nodes.description: Salvage for recurrent lower-grade glioma often begins with re-resection to confirm grade and rule out transformation, then selects the modality not yet given.
bullets: Re-resection where feasible confirms grade and rules out transformation to grade 4
Extent of safe re-resection again influences prognosis
Proceed to the modality step whether or not re-resection is performed

nodes.name: Recurrent LGG modality
nodes.title: Recurrent lower-grade glioma: modality by prior therapy
nodes.description: Choose the salvage modality by what has already been delivered and whether the tumor has transformed to higher grade.
bullets: Radiation-naive: focal radiation is the preferred next modality
Prior radiation: alkylating chemotherapy (temozolomide or PCV) is preferred
Transformed to grade 4 on re-resection: switch to the high-grade pathway

nodes.name: Recurrent LGG RT
nodes.title: Recurrent LGG, radiation-naive: focal radiation
nodes.description: A radiation-naive recurrent lower-grade glioma is salvaged with focal external-beam radiation, typically followed by chemotherapy.
bullets: Focal external-beam radiation to the recurrent tumor volume
Follow with alkylating chemotherapy (PCV for codeleted, temozolomide otherwise)
Baseline and serial neurocognitive assessment
The follow-on systemic regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts

nodes.name: Recurrent LGG chemo
nodes.title: Recurrent LGG, prior radiation: alkylating chemotherapy
nodes.description: When radiation has already been delivered, alkylating chemotherapy is the preferred salvage for recurrent lower-grade glioma.
bullets: Alkylating chemotherapy: temozolomide, or PCV (procarbazine, lomustine, vincristine)
Choose backbone by molecular class and prior tolerance
Monitor marrow counts and cumulative nitrosourea exposure
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts

nodes.name: Recurrent LGG transformed
nodes.title: Recurrent LGG transformed to grade 4: high-grade salvage
nodes.description: A lower-grade glioma that has transformed to grade 4 on re-resection is treated on the high-grade / glioblastoma salvage pathway.
bullets: Treat as high-grade disease: maximal safe re-resection plus chemoradiation as feasible
Alkylator-based systemic therapy; bevacizumab for symptom / edema control
Prioritize a clinical trial
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts

nodes.name: Recurrent astro line
nodes.title: Recurrent grade 4 IDH-mut astrocytoma: re-treatment decision
nodes.description: Salvage of recurrent grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma mirrors recurrent glioblastoma but with generally better outcomes. Decide on re-resection / re-irradiation versus straight to systemic salvage.
bullets: Re-resection for accessible, symptomatic recurrence; re-irradiation in selected cases
Alkylator-based systemic therapy (temozolomide rechallenge or lomustine)
Generally better prognosis than IDH-wildtype recurrence; clinical trial encouraged

nodes.name: Recurrent astro first salvage
nodes.title: Recurrent astrocytoma G4: first salvage systemic therapy
nodes.description: First-line salvage systemic therapy is an alkylator; the next decision depends on whether disease responds or progresses.
nodes.path: CNS / Recurrence / Astro G4 / First salvage
bullets: Temozolomide rechallenge (esp. MGMT-methylated with a treatment-free interval) or lomustine
Assess response by MRI after 2-3 cycles
Continue supportive care; manage seizures and edema
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts

options.label: Poor performance status - best supportive care

nodes.name: Recurrent astro later salvage
nodes.title: Recurrent astrocytoma G4: later-line salvage
nodes.description: After progression on first salvage, options are an alternate alkylator, bevacizumab for symptom control, or a clinical trial.
bullets: Alternate alkylator (switch temozolomide <-> lomustine) if not exhausted
Bevacizumab helps edema / steroid-refractory symptoms
Re-irradiation for focal recurrence in selected patients; prioritize a clinical trial
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts

nodes.name: Recurrent astro BSC
nodes.title: Recurrent astrocytoma G4: best supportive care
nodes.description: For poor performance status, best supportive care with symptom-directed measures is appropriate.
bullets: Symptom-directed care: steroids for edema, anti-seizure medication, analgesia
Palliative care / hospice referral as appropriate
Bevacizumab may be used purely for symptom control in selected patients
Best supportive care; no systemic dose protocol applies here (bevacizumab, if used for symptom control, is referenced on the salvage nodes)

nodes.name: Recurrent GBM resectable
nodes.title: Recurrent glioblastoma: resectability
nodes.description: For recurrent glioblastoma, whether the recurrence is safely resectable steers toward re-operation versus straight-to-systemic therapy / re-irradiation.

nodes.name: Recurrent GBM re-op
nodes.title: Recurrent GBM, resectable: re-resection then systemic
nodes.description: A focal, symptomatic, safely resectable glioblastoma recurrence is re-operated, optionally with a local implant, then moves to first-line salvage systemic therapy.
bullets: Re-resection for symptomatic mass effect / focal recurrence
Consider a locally implanted carmustine wafer at re-operation in selected cases
Then proceed to first-line salvage systemic therapy and/or re-irradiation
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts

nodes.name: Recurrent GBM first salvage
nodes.title: Recurrent GBM: first-line salvage systemic therapy
nodes.description: First-line salvage for recurrent glioblastoma is systemic therapy (with re-irradiation in selected cases); the next step depends on response versus further progression.
bullets: Systemic options: bevacizumab (edema / symptom control), lomustine, or temozolomide rechallenge (esp. MGMT-methylated with a treatment-free interval)
Re-irradiation for focal recurrence in selected patients
Assess response by MRI after 2 cycles; prioritize a clinical trial
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts

options.label: Poor performance status - best supportive care

nodes.name: Recurrent GBM later salvage
nodes.title: Recurrent GBM: later-line salvage
nodes.description: After progression on first salvage, later-line options are an alternate systemic agent or combination, with clinical trial strongly preferred.
bullets: Switch systemic agent: bevacizumab +/- lomustine, or an alternate alkylator if not exhausted
Consider re-irradiation for a focal, previously untreated volume
Clinical trial strongly preferred at this line
Recommended regimen(s) reference the CNS draft dose protocol(s) below, which compute per-drug doses in the Protocol Sheet; the physician confirms and adjusts

nodes.name: Recurrent GBM BSC
nodes.title: Recurrent GBM: best supportive care
nodes.description: For poor performance status at recurrence, best supportive care with symptom-directed measures is appropriate.
bullets: Symptom-directed care: steroids for edema, anti-seizure medication, analgesia
Bevacizumab may be used purely for steroid-refractory symptom control
Palliative care / hospice referral as appropriate
Best supportive care; no systemic dose protocol applies here (bevacizumab, if used for symptom control, is referenced on the salvage nodes)
